newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends weak on NYMEX expiry, poor margins.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends weak on NYMEX expiry, poor margins.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended weak on Tuesday, dragged down by the expiring NYMEX June contract and a reversal of midafternoon gains on U.S. products which refocussed attention on refining margins.
July Brent closed 14 cents lower at $20.02 a barrel, 18 cents above the low but well below the session high of $20.36 a barrel.
"The (NYMEX) June contract pulled the front end lower but after this afternoon's short-covering, U.S. products have been unable to hold their ground and that's added to the pressure," said a broker.

Brent rallied midafternoon, wiping out early session losses, as news of an attack by Kurdish rebels on a small oil installation in southern Turkey provided enough momentum to take the contract through resistance at $20.08 a barrel.
Short-covering on U.S. crude and gasoline helped lift Brent to a new intraday high but the gains soon evaporated as products turned tail again, adding to pressure on refiners' margins.
Returns at some European plants have dipped into the red this week and several are considering cutting crude throughput.
Technical resistance at $20.36 a barrel also capped July's rally, dealers said.

Markets were also nervous ahead of the release of American Petroleum Institute (API) stocks data due out after the close on Tuesday. Last week, the API reported a surprise massive build in crude stocks.
Earlier, IPE gas oil futures closed unchanged, June ending at $177.75 a tonne.
June/July slipped further into contango as the July contract closed 50 cents firmer at $179.50 a tonne.
